verses.text: The elder, to the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in truth; and not I only, but also all those who know the truth;
for the truth’s sake, which remains in us, and it will be with us forever:
Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
I rejoice greatly that I have found some of your children walking in truth, even as we have been commanded by the Father.
Now I beg you, dear lady, not as though I wrote to you a new commandment, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.
This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, even as you heard from the beginning, that you should walk in it.
For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who don’t confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. This is the deceiver and the Antichrist.
Watch yourselves, that we don’t lose the things which we have accomplished, but that we receive a full reward.
Whoever transgresses and doesn’t remain in the teaching of Christ, doesn’t have God. He who remains in the teaching, the same has both the Father and the Son.
If anyone comes to you, and doesn’t bring this teaching, don’t receive him into your house, and don’t welcome him,
for he who welcomes him participates in his evil deeds.
Having many things to write to you, I don’t want to do so with paper and ink, but I hope to come to you, and to speak face to face, that our joy may be made full.
The children of your chosen sister greet you. Amen.

footnotes.content: The elder writes to 'the chosen lady'—and I've always found something tender in this. She's real, she's known, she's loved not because of title but because she holds fast to the truth of Jesus. Love in truth is not sentimental; it's clear-eyed, rooted in who Christ is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Truth is not fleeting—it remains in us and will be with us forever. In a world that shifts and bends, here is a promise that steadies the soul. The Lord Himself is that truth, and He does not change.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Grace, mercy, peace—the greeting echoes Paul's letters, yet here the elder adds a weighty phrase: 'in truth and love.' It's not blessing poured out carelessly, but blessing rooted in Jesus Christ Himself, the Son of the Father. A grandparent's blessing to a beloved child.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What makes an old pastor's heart rejoice? Watching the young walk in truth—obedient to the Father's command, steady and sure. This is more precious than any other news; the faith is being lived out in the next generation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The elder says this isn't new, but oh, how we need to hear it afresh. Love one another—it's the heartbeat of the faith, ancient as the beginning, yet we drift from it daily. A simple, hard commandment that costs us everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Love isn't feeling; it's obedience. It's walking according to His commandments, not the world's. That narrow road of faith—'walk in it'—takes all our will, all our trust, all our love focused on Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Many deceivers—in every age. They deny that Jesus came in the flesh, that He became human, died, rose again. To deny this is to stand against Christ Himself. We must see with clear eyes: these are not small errors, but the work of the Antichrist spirit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Watch yourselves—there's a weight here. What we've accomplished in Christ is fragile only if we stop watching, stop holding fast. Our reward is full in Him, but we must not grow careless and drift from truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To leave the teaching of Christ is to lose the Father and the Son both. It's not a technicality—it's the whole faith. Remain in Him; abide in His word. That's where the life is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The elder calls the church to discernment and protection. Don't receive those who bring false teaching into your home. Hospitality is precious, but truth comes first. Love sometimes means saying no.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To welcome a deceiver is to become complicit—you participate in their evil. Sharp words, but true. We are responsible for what we harbor, what we encourage, what we lend our voice to.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paper and ink won't do for this. The elder longs for face-to-face presence—to see the beloved lady, to speak heart to heart. Even our words in writing fall short of the joy that comes when we gather in Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this simple closing: we too are 'chosen,' and those loved by Christ greet us in faith. From John's sister church, through the centuries, to us—the communion of the saints continues.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
